title: Consistent REST-API problem
body:
Hello:

I don´t know why but from today I'm receiving consistent error messages (pop-up) on my Android smartphone. I attach a photo showing the error. What can I do?

Thank you in advance. 

![screenshot_20180403-141937](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26350345/38262479-3485db16-3765-11e8-8bfd-7bdcb5b4822b.png)

comments.body: I'm having the same exact issue.
Not sure of any resolution at this point.  I've tried all the standard things... restarting azure site, rebooting phone, etc. with no positive change.
Yes, it's annoying, in 4 hours I have had this error 300 times. I was thinking to restart all what you did but if it doesn't work, no idea what will do.
This is such an odd issue.  I see some of my BG readings going through to Nightscout but it's very sporadic and very laggy and none of my treatments show up in nightscout.
It looks like something has systematically changed with the REST API env but I have no idea what that is or how to troubleshoot it.

carloslpa... I've got a workaround... per this alert article:  https://app.azure.com/h/_1KC-RQ0/6807cc

Follow that, then replace https with http in your rest api cloud upload url in xdrip+, then restart your azure site... on the next nightscout upload, all your readings and treatments should go in.

Hello gitanO0

I cannot open that url, it readdress me directly to the main page of azure. 

But some minutes ago, I went to my azure profile and I got a message from the system showing that I had a problem and I followed the steps, and aparently I solved the problem because of my nightscout URL didn't work from yesterday, and now it is working, let's see if I receive the pop-up error on my xDrip+

I copy the message:

_Starting at 02:00 UTC on 3 Apr 2018, you have been identified as a customer using App Services who may have received connection failure notifications when using Android apps with older HTTP clients or desktop browsers using cross-site scripting calls. Engineers have identified an issue with a recent deployment and are investigating mitigation options. Customers experiencing this issue can self-mitigate by updating the site config setting "http20Enabled" to false via resources.azure.com. Instructions on how to update site config can be found here: https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/azure-resource-explorer-a-new-tool-to-discover-the-azure-api/

1) Go to https://resources.azure.com/  

2) Make sure you are in Read/Write mode by clicking in the option to the left of your name.  

3) Find the affected site and browse to Config > Web: https://resources.azure.com/subscriptions/<yourSubscriptionId>/resourceGroups/<yourWebAppResourceGroup>/providers/Microsoft.Web/sites/<yourWebAppName>/config/web  

4) Change the property: "http20Enabled": from true to false by clicking in Edit properties, Update to “false” and then clicking PUT to save change. 

If you have tried these steps and are continuing to experience issues with your App Service, please create a technical support ticket to further troubleshoot: aka.ms/azsupt. This message will be closed in 7 days._
Yes, that's the same thing I did.  I wouldn't close this but at least there's a workaround.

Hellow. I had the same problem to upload my son's data using blucon and xdrip plus, but this solution have worked. Thank you so much!
I also found a similar answer to this problem at:
https://social.msdn.microsoft.com/Forums/azure/en-US/dd36a177-e9c4-4ced-af48-8e327accf70f/failure-establishing-a-connection-to-azure-app-service-from-android-apps-or-older-http-clients?forum=windowsazurewebsitespreview
Thank you very very much!
